abilitygroupdescription.p: The primary abilities are five core abilities that represent the characters raw, innate, unlearned capabilities. sec:primary_abilities

Checks Ability
Ability Check
Primary Ability Check
Primary Ability Checks are ability checks, made using one of the characters primary abilities, Strength, Endurance, Agility, etc. Primary Ability checks are usually used when no more specific check can be applied, a character might check using their Agility when trying to catch a falling object as there is no catch ability. A check whether a character can make it to shore from a sinking ship should be made using the Swim ability and not the endurance primary ability, since the Swim ability is more specific in this case.

playexample.p: Dourli tries to shift a large wine barrel that is sitting on a trap door in a cellar. The GM declares that in order to do so Dourli must make a Strength Check with a difficulty of 12. The player rolls a 9 for their Outcome. Dourli has Strength 2, and so gets a total of 11. Dourli fails to move the wine barrel. If he had a Strength 3 he would have succeeded.

abilitydescription.p: Represents the characters brute physical power. Strength savs are made when the character wishes to perform a Feat of Strength, such as bending bars, opening doors and to lift heavy objects. Strength modifies melee damage and the characters Health.

Endurance
Abilities Endurance
The characters ability to handle physical stress. If a character has a high Endurance it indicates that they are healthy and tough. Endurance is used to oppose poisons, resist exhaustion, diseases, the cold, and modifies the characters Stamina.

Agility
Abilities Agility
Acrobatics (use Agility)
The characters ability to move easily; their nimbleness, athleticism and dexterity. Agility modifies the characters Dodge Checks.
The Sure-Feet specialization is used when the attacker the character would be knocked prone.

ability.slug: Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast.

abilitydescription.p:
Speed
Abilities Speed
Movement see Speed
Jumping (use Speed)
Speed represents how physically fast the character is. Speed checks should be made for characters attempting to sprint, jump, or fleeing.

Perception
Abilities Perception
Spot Hidden use Perception
Initiative see Perception
Notice (use Perception)
Listen (use Perception)
The character's awareness, acumen and insight. Perception represents your attentiveness to detail and your unflagging vigilance. In game this value is used socially, for reading people and detecting underhanded motives. Perception modifies checks used both for surveying the surrounds for potential avenues of attack, and reduces the likelihood of being surprised, for searching.
Perception can be used in social situations to see if a person is being deceptive.

abilitycountercheck.fail: Another local ally makes a mettle check.

abilitydescription.p:
Will
Abilities Will
Will represents the characters strength of character. Their grit and determination. Will is often used when making Mettle Checks.
Characters may, from time to time, be forced to make a Mettle Check. Mettle Checks occur when characters have to face their fears.

A Mettle Check is a check made against the Mettle Pool. It has a Toll of 1 and a DDC of 6. When a character fails a Mettle Check another neraby character, chosen at random or by the GM, must also make a Mettle Check. Mettle checks can continue to cascade until someone succeeds or everyone has failed a Mettle Check. Mettle Checks are free actions.

The GM should feel free to modify the Mettle Check DC as he pleases, to reflect being attacked at night, being vastly outnumbered, the horrible visage of the characters opponents, the party being in good spirits etc. As characters fail Mettle Checks the party starts to lose dice from their Mettle Pools and their fighting options become somewhat diminished.

Some suggested times to make Mettle Checks are:
Whenever a party member becomes Bloodied,
When the party enters combat against a Fear causing opponent,
Whenever the party is Surprised or Ambushed.
Ultimately, however, it is up to the GMs discretion to decide when the players should make a Mettle check and the GM should feel free to force Mettle Checks sooner or later in the combat to satisfy the narrative imperative.

The first time the group collectively fails a Mettle Check then everyone gains the Checked Condition see pagecondition:checked, after the second time everyone fails a Mettle Check everyone gains the Broken Condition, see pagecondition:broken. The third time the group fails their Mettle Check they gain the Routed Condition, see pagecondition:routed.

Had Dourli rolled a 19/1 he would have initially succeeded, then since his Luck Pool would have been reduced below zero, it's set to zero and he fails the check for want of Luck.

abilitydescription.p: Some abilities target the opponents Mettle, Banish, and Howl of the Hunt. In these circumstances the character makes a check against their targets Mettle, and if successfully deducts a cost, specified by the ability being used, from their opponents Mettle pool.

Magic Resilience
Characters make a magic check to overcome the effects of magic cast against them.

Luck Check
Characters make a luck check to see if fortune smiles on them.

Luck Checks
Checks Luck
Whenever the GM finds themselves in a situation where they turn to a player and ask Do you feel lucky? then perhaps the player should be making a Luck Check. A Luck Check is a check made against the Luck Pool.

playexample.p: Dourli is sitting in a corner tied up by the Black Mark, waiting on an uncertain fate. A lone guard, in his cups, watches over him. Dourli wonders whether the guard might need to leave momentarily to relieve himself. The GM determines that since Dourli has been tied up for a long time and the the guard is drinking, chances are high that the guard will leave the room for a short time at some point. So he sets an easy DC for the check of 7. The GM asks Dourli whether he's feelling lucky? Dourli's current Luck Pool is 1. He rolls and gets a 17. Dourli's Luck pool is reduced by one to zero. Dourli takes his opportunity when the guard leaves and bolts for it, his arms still tied.
